title: Crew French Toast Bake
subtitle: Cinnamon French toast baked in a 9x13 for clean slices.
description: Day-old bread soaked in cinnamon custard, baked in a 9x13, and sliced into squares. Maple syrup on the side — easier than standing at the griddle for an hour.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Crew French Toast Bake in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch Eggs. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Heat the oven
steps.instruction: Heat oven to 375°F. Grease a deep 9x13 pan. Allow 10–15 minutes for mise en place before heat goes on. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Build the pan
steps.instruction: Spread bread cubes evenly. Whisk eggs, milk, sugar, cinnamon, vanilla, and melted butter; pour over bread. Press gently so all cubes soak.

steps.title: Bake until set
steps.instruction: Bake until the center is set and the top is golden. If the center jiggles like loose custard, bake 5 more minutes. Bake until the center reaches a safe internal temp (165°F) and edges look set — use a thermometer at the thickest point. Plan about 35 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Crew French Toast Bake onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Scale for larger halls
steps.instruction: When cooking for more than 8 firefighters, split into two pans halfway through so the bottom layer does not overcook while the top waits — duplicate mise en place if you double batches.

steps.title: Rest and slice
steps.instruction: Rest 10 minutes for clean squares. Serve with maple syrup. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

stationWorkflow: Assign one cook to the hot surface and one to assembly. Keep the line moving; don’t crowd the griddle.
Set a warm holding zone (oven 200°F or covered hotel pan) so staggered eaters still get a hot plate.
Run a quick call-proof check: anything crispy stays uncovered; anything soft stays covered.
cleanupNotes: While plates are served, scrape the griddle/pan and wipe with a damp towel (use tongs + folded towel).
Soak the mixing bowl and sheet pan immediately—breakfast starch sets fast when it cools.
leftovers: Cool fast: spread on a sheet pan 10 minutes, then portion into containers so it doesn’t sweat.
Reheat rule: eggs reheat best covered at 50% power or low oven heat; don’t nuke on high.
